## One important adjustment to the MainConfig idea

Your goal is right: one understandable place for editable settings. But it should not work by “automatically scanning every C# file and guessing which variables are configuration.”

That would become dangerous and confusing because the game cannot reliably know whether a value is:

- a safe editable setting;
- a temporary runtime state;
- an internal timer;
- an entity handle;
- a gameplay constant that should not be exposed;
- content data such as a ped model, station, weapon, crime definition, or gang entry.

The maintainable version of your design is:

```text
Each system explicitly declares the settings it allows the player to edit
→ LSImmersiveMainConfig registers and validates those settings
→ LSImmersiveMainUI.xml stores them in clear named sections
→ LSMainSetting / LSImmersiveHotkeys display and edit them
→ the owning system reads its typed section
```

So a Dispatch system could explicitly declare:

```text
Dispatch.Enabled
Dispatch.QuietPatrolMinimumSeconds
Dispatch.QuietPatrolMaximumSeconds
Dispatch.GlobalCooldownSeconds
Dispatch.RepeatProtectionMinutes
Dispatch.MaximumActiveIncidents
Dispatch.SceneSpawnDistance
Dispatch.AudioEnabled
Dispatch.AudioMinimumGapSeconds
```

The NPC system could explicitly declare:

```text
NpcResponse.Enabled
NpcResponse.InteractionRadius
NpcResponse.TrafficStopRadius
NpcResponse.LocalTrafficAwarenessRadius
NpcResponse.CollisionGuardCooldownSeconds
NpcResponse.MaximumTrafficVehiclesAffected
NpcResponse.CitizenReactionEnabled
NpcResponse.VehicleStopTimeoutSeconds
```

The Convoy system could explicitly declare:

```text
Convoy.Enabled
Convoy.TransportVehicleModel
Convoy.StationArrivalRadius
Convoy.PrisonArrivalRadius
Convoy.PrisonerRecoveryTimeoutSeconds
Convoy.AllowTerminalCompletion
```

The systems still own the meaning and validation of those values. `LSImmersiveMainConfig` owns the single XML file, loading, saving, preserving sections, and presenting a clean overview.

That prevents every gameplay file from generating its own random `.ini` or XML file while also preventing one massive C# configuration class with hundreds of unrelated hard-coded fields.

## The correct MainConfig boundary

Your existing [`LSImmersiveMainConfig.cs`](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSImmersiveMainConfig.cs:14>) already has the beginning of this idea, but it is currently much smaller than your mapping.

It currently handles only:

- Main menu toggle key;
- audio enabled;
- audio volume;
- Police keyboard bindings.

Its current persisted XML is also very small:

```xml
<Controls menuToggle="F4" />
<Audio enabled="true" volume="55" />
<PoliceControls ... />
```

See [LSImmersiveMainUI.xml](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSImmersiveMainUI.xml:1>).

The current source explicitly keeps much Police configuration outside the main config file, especially in [`LSPDImmersiveProfile.xml`](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSPDImmersiveProfile.xml:1>). That conflicts with the architecture you have now defined.

The intended future structure should remain one main settings XML, while keeping **content catalogs** separate. For example:

```xml
<LSImmersiveMainUI version="2">

  <Universal>
    <Interface menuToggle="F4" />
    <Audio enabled="true" volume="55" />
    <Logging runtimeEnabled="true"
             debugEnabled="true"
             sessionHeaders="true"
             verboseDiagnostics="false" />
  </Universal>

  <Controls>
    <Universal menuToggle="F4" />
    <Police patrol="P"
            accept="Y"
            reject="N"
            investigate="I"
            secure="E"
            transport="R"
            transportComplete="T"
            interaction="G"
            backup="B"
            reset="F10" />
  </Controls>

  <Police>
    <Authority suppressWantedLevel="true"
               preventVanillaPoliceHostility="true"
               preserveNormalCivilianLife="true" />

    <Patrol enabled="true"
            reuseCurrentPoliceVehicle="true"
            preventDuplicatePersonalVehicle="true" />

    <Dispatch enabled="true"
              minQuietPatrolSeconds="180"
              maxQuietPatrolSeconds="600"
              repeatProtectionMinutes="20"
              maxActiveIncidents="1"
              audioMinimumGapSeconds="5" />

    <NPCResponse enabled="true"
                 trafficAwarenessRadius="28"
                 collisionGuardCooldownMilliseconds="1200"
                 maximumAffectedTrafficVehicles="3"
                 pedestrianInteractionRadius="4.5" />

    <ResponseUnits enabled="true"
                   allowBackup="true"
                   automaticPursuitSupport="true"
                   maxUnitsPerIncident="1" />

    <Convoy enabled="true"
            transportVehicleModel="fbi2"
            stationArrivalRadius="24"
            prisonArrivalRadius="32"
            terminalCompletionEnabled="true" />

    <Cleanup completedSceneGraceSeconds="90"
             hardCleanupSeconds="900" />
  </Police>

  <Developer enabled="false"
             diagnosticOverlay="false"
             entityOwnershipOverlay="false" />

</LSImmersiveMainUI>
```

This does **not** mean every XML file should be merged into one giant file.

These should remain separate data sources because they are content catalogs, not ordinary user settings:

- [`LSPDDispatchEvent.xml`](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSPDDispatchEvent.xml:1>) — Dispatch callout definitions;
- [`LSPDCrimeActivityEvent.xml`](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSPDCrimeActivityEvent.xml:1>) — Crime Activity data;
- Police ped, vehicle, weapon, station, and profile collections;
- `ResponseAudio.xml` — audio catalog and clips;
- external Gang & Turf data — read-only external gameplay data.

The Main Config should store **how the systems behave**, while the existing catalog XML files store **what content exists**.

## LSImmersiveLog is the correct universal logging owner

Your understanding of [`LSImmersiveLog.cs`](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSImmersiveLog.cs:11>) is correct.

It should be the one universal logging service used throughout the whole project, not only Police Mode.

The intended distinction should be strict:

| Log | What belongs there |
|---|---|
| `LSRuntime.log` | Verified gameplay actions, mode entry/exit, Dispatch state changes, NPC interaction stages, entity ownership changes, arrival confirmation, cleanup, user commands, selected models, completed outcomes |
| `LSDebug.log` | Failed entity validation, invalid config, unsupported model, missing animation dictionary, native task failure, state-machine mismatch, lost suspect, prisoner ownership failure, failed vehicle seat assignment, unexpected cleanup, caught exception |

The current logger class has the correct two-file structure:

- `Runtime()` writes to `LSRuntime.log`;
- `Debug()` and `Exception()` write to `LSDebug.log`.

See [LSImmersiveLog.cs](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSImmersiveLog.cs:50>).

However, your concern is valid: the current logging use is incomplete.

For example, the recent broken custody flow writes this to Runtime:

```text
POLICE_CUSTODY_FAILED | The prisoner is no longer available for custody.
```

But it does not write enough matching diagnostic evidence to `LSDebug.log` explaining:

- the prisoner handle;
- whether the ped still existed;
- whether the ped was dead;
- whether the ped was in the intended vehicle;
- which seat was requested;
- whether the transport vehicle existed;
- whether Dispatch still owned the ped;
- whether another system deleted or reassigned it;
- what custody state was active at the moment of failure.

That is why the Runtime log tells us **that** the transport failed, but Debug does not tell us **why** it failed.

The current logger also appends every session into the same two files. It has boot records, but it does not yet have a clean session identifier, session header, session-end summary, archive policy, or rotation policy. That makes multi-day debugging harder than it needs to be.

A good runtime session header would look like:

```text
SESSION_STARTED
SessionId=20260909-153422-7F3A
ScriptVersion=...
Build=Debug
GameBuild=...
SHVDN=3.9.0
ActiveRole=None
```

A session end or recovery record could look like:

```text
SESSION_SUMMARY
DispatchesOffered=3
DispatchesAccepted=1
ArrestsCompleted=1
CustodyFailures=1
NPCInteractionsStarted=4
NPCInteractionsCompleted=1
ResponseUnitsRequested=0
UnhandledExceptions=0
```

That would make it much easier for you to identify whether a gameplay session is improving or getting worse.

There is also a practical performance concern: the current logger writes synchronously to disk. The recent log showed repeated `NPC_TRAFFIC_COLLISION_GUARD` entries roughly every fraction of a second. That does not prove it caused the freeze, but high-frequency file writing on the game thread is avoidable pressure. Runtime logs should record meaningful transitions, while repeated scans should be sampled, aggregated, or written only when the result changes.

## The architecture contract I will follow

When implementation resumes, I will keep these rules:

1. `LSIMMERSIVEUI.cs` remains the universal front door. It does not gain Dispatch, Convoy, arrest, gang, NPC, or Police AI logic.

2. `LSRoleplay.cs` remains a simple role-category selector. It does not activate or manage Police gameplay directly.

3. `LSAuthorityRole.cs` remains a selected-mode router. It does not become a new Police Core and does not contain Dispatch or Convoy rules.

4. `LSImmersivePoliceUI.cs` presents contextual Police controls and forwards deliberate commands to `LSImmersivePoliceCore`.

5. `LSImmersivePoliceCore.cs` coordinates Police-owned systems, but Dispatch, Convoy, NPC Response, Gang integration, Audio, Patrol, and Response Units keep their own specialized logic.

6. `LSImmersiveMainConfig.cs` becomes the central persisted configuration registry for all deliberately exposed settings.

7. `LSImmersiveHotkeys.cs` becomes the universal editable controls interface.

8. `LSMainSetting.cs` becomes the universal editable settings interface.

9. Each gameplay system owns its typed settings validation, but no gameplay system silently creates another user-facing configuration file.

10. `LSImmersiveLog.cs` receives both runtime transitions and diagnostic evidence from every active owner.

11. Runtime logs record confirmed actions. Debug logs record failures, unexpected states, invalid data, native-task failures, and recovery actions.

12. High-frequency loops do not spam disk logs every few hundred milliseconds.

This mapping is strong and maintainable. It gives you one understandable center for settings and controls without turning one massive file into the gameplay brain or destroying the existing specialized Police systems.

### The main UI is now a gateway, not a Police gameplay brain

### Runtime and debug logging are separated

runtime entries

|---|---|

| Audio | Main Settings enable/volume are applied to the shared Police audio owner |

The existing Dispatch owner now keeps Dispatch sparse and does not create overlapping calls:

- Dispatch is disabled from generating new offers if disabled in Main Settings.
- The next offer uses the configured quiet-patrol range.
- Previously offered definitions are held back for the configured repeat-protection window.
- `maximumActiveIncidents` is deliberately normalized to **one**. The UI presents that as a read-only design rule instead of pretending that several concurrent Dispatch incidents are supported.

### Custody and transport failure recovery were improved

[LSPDConvoy.cs](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSPDConvoy.cs:332>) no longer immediately destroys the whole transport chain if the prisoner is temporarily unavailable.

It now:

1. Detects the missing prisoner.
2. Records `POLICE_CUSTODY_PRISONER_RECOVERY_WAIT` in Runtime logs.
3. Waits for the configurable recovery timeout.
4. Fails only after the recovery period expires.

A confirmed dead prisoner still follows the appropriate failure path. This is intended to prevent an ordinary transient entity problem from instantly collapsing custody/transport gameplay.

The terminal transport completion command uses the configurable centralized control rather than hardcoding `T` in the convoy owner.

### GPS behavior is now consistently controlled

The universal **Show Waypoint** setting now affects:

- Dispatch waypoint placement
- Custody/transport waypoint placement
- Station routing
- Crime-intelligence routing
- Starting patrol toward the selected station

When route guidance is disabled, the underlying incident, patrol, transport, or intelligence state remains valid. The system simply does not place a new GPS waypoint.

## Police Authority behavior developed

[LSPDAuthority.cs](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSPDAuthority.cs:16>) is now the dedicated Police Authority session boundary.

When Police Authority is active, it now does the following through verified ScriptHookVDotNet native hashes:

- Captures the player’s current wanted level and maximum wanted-level limit before applying Police Authority behavior.
- Enables `SET_POLICE_IGNORE_PLAYER` for the active Police player.
- Disables vanilla GTA Police dispatch against the active Police player through `SET_DISPATCH_COPS_FOR_PLAYER`.
- Temporarily sets the maximum wanted level to zero while the Authority setting is enabled.
- Clears an actual wanted level only when one exists, rather than repeatedly clearing it every tick.
- Rechecks Authority protection at a configurable interval, defaulting to `750` milliseconds.
- Restores the captured wanted/max-wanted state when Police Authority ends.
- Restores vanilla Police-ignore and Police-dispatch behavior when Police Authority ends.
- Keeps all of this inside the Authority lifecycle: entering Police Authority starts the protection; leaving Police Authority restores GTA behavior.

This directly targets the issues you reported:

- Wanted stars appearing, disappearing, and returning while Police Mode is active.
- Vanilla Police dispatch continuing to treat the player as a criminal.
- Vanilla officers repeatedly raising/lowering weapons because they still consider the player hostile.
- Police Authority appearing active in the UI while GTA’s Police logic still behaves as if Venti is a normal civilian.

I explicitly did **not** use:

- `SET_EVERYONE_IGNORE_PLAYER`
- `SET_RELATIONSHIP_BETWEEN_GROUPS`
- `SET_PED_RELATIONSHIP_GROUP_HASH`

So this is not an “ignored by everyone” system, and it does not globally rewrite gang/civilian/Police relationship groups. It preserves the separate Gang & Turf, vanilla gang, civilian, Dispatch, and NPC systems.

## Nearby Police and military support developed

[LSPDPoliceResponse.cs](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSPDPoliceResponse.cs:260>) now owns a separate local Authority-support pass.

`LSPDAuthority` does **not** scan or task ambient peds. `LSPDPoliceResponse` performs that narrow nearby-officer behavior, and [LSImmersivePoliceCore.cs](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSImmersivePoliceCore.cs:259>) only coordinates the call.

While Police Authority is active, the response owner:

- Scans only the configurable local radius around the player.
- Recognizes Police through the GTA `Cop` relationship group, Police vehicles, and a narrow fallback list of known Police models.
- Recognizes Arm

y/base personnel through the GTA `Army` relationship group and a narrow fallback list of known military models.
- Does **not** classify civilians, vanilla gangs, Gang & Turf members, or Anyiii companions as Authority allies.
- Checks whether a recognised officer is actually in combat against Police Anyi.
- Clears that officer’s current hostile task only when the officer is specifically targeting the player.
- Gives idle, nearby recognised officers a short visual acknowledgement through a lightweight look-at task.
- Does not delete, persist, adopt, change relationship groups, or otherwise take ownership of ambient GTA peds.
- Gives hostile officers priority over cosmetic acknowledgements, so idle Police greetings cannot consume the limited support budget while another nearby officer is aiming at the player.

The local support flow is intentionally restrained:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Active[Police Authority active]
    Authority[LSPDAuthority applies player protection]
    Core[Police Core coordinates owners]
    Scan[LSPDPoliceResponse scans nearby Police / Army only]
    Hostile{Officer targeting<br/>Police player?}
    Clear[Clear hostile task locally]
    Acknowledge[Brief officer acknowledgement]
    Ignore[Leave civilian, gang, and unrelated entities alone]

    Active --> Authority --> Core --> Scan
    Scan --> Hostile
    Hostile -->|Yes| Clear
    Hostile -->|No, idle nearby officer| Acknowledge
    Scan --> Ignore
```

The existing Dispatch response-unit and backup system remains separate. A spawned backup unit still needs an active Dispatch or gang situation, while nearby vanilla Police recognition works during ordinary Police patrol too.

## What was developed

Crime Activity now follows this gameplay flow:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Police Authority + Patrol] --> B[Quiet nearby Crime intelligence]
    B --> C[Tip appears near the authored area]
    C --> D{Officer chooses}
    D -->|Ignore| E[Location + redeployment cooldown]
    D -->|GPS / travel| F[Begin nearby investigation]
    F --> G[Owned criminal scene and behavior]
    G --> H{Officer response}
    H -->|Confront| I[Criminals flee or fight]
    H -->|Request Backup| J[Backup stages and drives to scene]
    J --> I
    I --> K[Scene contained, criminals gone, or group disperses]
    K --> L[Grace-period cleanup + Patrol resumes]
```

The separation from Dispatch is enforced in the Core:

- Crime Activity discovery only runs during a quiet Police Patrol.
- A Crime Activity **tip** is passive intelligence. It does not create a Dispatch offer, GPS route, criminal scene, Backup request, or urgent incident by itself.
- An actual Crime Activity starts only after the player chooses **Begin Current Investigation** near the selected location.
- While a Crime Activity scene is active, Dispatch, Convoy, Gang incidents, NPC interaction, and new Backup assignments are prevented from overlapping it.
- If a Dispatch, Convoy, Gang incident, NPC interaction, or Backup assignment becomes active while a passive Crime tip exists, the tip remains available in the UI but stays silent. It will not post a notification or play audio over the other activity.
- Closing, ignoring, abandoning, or resolving Crime Activity defers new Dispatch offers for a short context-clear period.

The new real scene behavior includes:

- One owned Crime Activity scene at a time.
- Asynchronous model preparation with a configurable timeout; there is no `Script.Wait` inside menu callbacks.
- Configurable **2–6** owned criminal participants and an optional authored scene vehicle.
- Actual GTA ped tasks using the project’s already-used `TASK_START_SCENARIO_IN_PLACE` native.
- Event-specific visual behavior driven by the XML event’s authored stages and ped roles:
  - reconnaissance, planning, vehicle preparation, and route observation use clipboard / planning behavior;
  - cargo, package, transfer, storage, and vehicle scenes use role-aware activity behavior;
  - lookouts, guards, and security use local guard-style behavior;
  - meetings and lower-risk gatherings use different idle/meeting scenario behavior.
- Nearby participants look toward other members rather than remaining as unassigned statue peds.
- Officer confrontation or actual gunfire escalates the scene into GTA flee/combat behavior.
- Backup only escalates the scene after officers have physically arrived and exited their own response vehicles.
- A scene completes when all owned criminals are neutralized, disappear, or leave the configured activity area.
- Failed partial scene creation immediately removes only the entities created by Crime Activity, preventing stranded lone peds or vehicles.
- Completed Crime scenes remain briefly for aftermath, then only Crime Activity-owned peds and vehicles are cleaned using the existing grace-distance and hard-timeout cleanup behavior.

Crime Activity does **not** automatically become an arrest/Convoy/Prison case. That remains the Dispatch/custody chain. A Crime Activity is resolved as its own scene after the criminal group is contained, neutralized, or dispersed.

## Event data and ownership structure

The mapping is now aligned with the structure you described:

| Owner | Responsibility now implemented |
|---|---|
| `LSPDCrimeActivityEvent.cs` | Reads and validates `LSPDCrimeActivityEvent.xml`, selects a nearby off-cooldown activity, resolves its ped/weapon/vehicle resource sets, and never creates GTA entities. |
| `LSPDCrimeActivity.cs` | Owns the live scene, criminal entities, AI tasks, escalation, cooldowns, audio scopes, scene blip, aftermath cleanup, and final result. |
| `LSPDBackUp.cs` | Stages Police units safely, drives them toward the active Crime Activity, lets them arrive and exit vehicles, then supports the actual Crime Activity-owned suspects. |
| `LSImmersivePoliceCore.cs` | Coordinates all owners, applies the no-overlap rules, delegates UI commands, and prevents Crime Activity from becoming Dispatch. |
| `LSImmersivePoliceUI.cs` | Presents Criminal Activity status, intelligence, GPS, begin, confront, ignore/close, and database browsing. It does not own scene entities or gameplay state. |

The existing Crime Activity database remains the data source:

- **14** authored Crime Activity definitions
- **16** authored locations
- **5** criminal groups
- Existing ped, weapon, vehicle, location, territory, stage, and role data remains data-driven through [`LSPDCrimeActivityEvent.xml`](<C:/Users/Carl Gap/CodexWork/Anyi/LSImmersiveLife/LSPDCrimeActivityEvent.xml:5>)

idated by the Event owner, then used by `LSPDCrimeActivity` only after the officer deliberately begins a nearby investigation.

**1. What was developed**

- **Police-duty traffic protection now works outside active incidents.**
  - While Police Authority is active, the local collision-awareness system runs even before Patrol begins or between Police activities.
  - It examines only nearby vehicles that are actually moving toward the player.
  - Outside an active Police scene, only one immediate collision-risk vehicle is affected at a time.
  - An approaching vehicle has its speed reduced.
  - When it reaches the immediate collision zone, a short per-frame collision guard protects the player from being repeatedly launched into ragdoll.
  - The collision guard expires automatically and does not permanently disable collision.
  - Traffic elsewhere in Los Santos remains under normal GTA behavior.
  - No global `SET_EVERYONE_IGNORE_PLAYER` behavior was introduced.

- **Active Police scenes now produce localized civilian reactions.**
  - Nearby ordinary pedestrians can watch cautiously, move away, or flee according to whether there is aiming or actual gunfire.
  - Active gunfire produces a stronger response than merely holding or aiming a weapon.
  - Reactions are limited by configurable radius, pedestrian count, and per-civilian cooldown.
  - Approaching civilian drivers can slow and receive a real drive-away task instead of blindly continuing through the scene.
  - Scene traffic reactions are not continuously restarted every frame.
  - The old runtime-log pattern that repeatedly emitted `NPC_ACTIVE_SCENE_TRAFFIC_DEPARTURE` during an ordinary contact was addressed by separating a true active Police scene from a normal NPC interaction.

- **On-foot Police interaction is now a physical state sequence.**
  - A nearby ordinary civilian can notice the approaching officer.
  - Only one candidate is selected.
  - The candidate slows or stops near Anyi and turns toward the player.
  - Pressing the configured Interaction key begins the contact.
  - The civilian performs a real greeting gesture using `gestures@m@standing@casual / gesture_hello`.
  - The civilian performs a real identification hand-over gesture using `mp_common / givetake1_a`.
  - Animation dictionaries are requested asynchronously across game ticks.
  - The code waits for the dictionary to load before playing the animation.
  - If an animation cannot stream within three seconds, the interaction continues through a physical look-at fallback and records the failure in the Debug log.
  - The citizen waits for the officer’s decision instead of immediately returning to ambient walking.
  - The hold task is only renewed if the citizen actually starts moving away. It is no longer restarted every fraction of a second.
  - Agree/X releases the citizen and returns them to natural ambient behavior.
  - Disagree/O can produce either:
    - a fleeing citizen and active pursuit, or
    - a compliant citizen who raises their hands and waits for Backup transport.
  - A fleeing citizen receives a tracking blip.
  - If the citizen stops, the internal state changes to match what physically happened instead of claiming they are still fleeing.

- **Traffic stops now use one selected driver and a controlled pull-over lifecycle.**
  

- The project observes the existing horn/siren control through `VehicleHorn`.
  - It does not activate, replace, or force a siren native.

  - One relevant driver is selected. Unrelated nearby traffic is not converted into traffic-stop subjects.

  - The pull-over task is issued once.

  - Once stopped, the driver remains seated and the vehicle is held with its handbrake.

  - The driver physically performs the document gesture while remaining inside the vehicle.
  - Agree/X releases the vehicle and restores driving behavior.

  - Flee behavior is given a real driving task and only one recovery task.
  - A stopped fleeing vehicle transitions back into a contained contact instead of continuing to display false “driver fled” text.

### What I found and repaired

The September 11 runtime confirms the problem very clearly. Immediately after Police Authority starts, Profile assets are queued while wanted-cap enforcement and NPC collision guards are already firing repeatedly.  A traffic interaction then reaches `NPC_TRAFFIC_CONTACT_STARTED`, but shortly afterward the context becomes quiet without reaching the expected pull-over/document progression. 

The largest internal problem was Profile streaming. I parsed **8,778 Debug entries**; **8,670 were weapon-asset-load-pending messages**, plus repeated vehicle/ped pending messages and Profile timeouts. The log shows the same weapon collection being requested repeatedly immediately before a Profile timeout, then more vehicle/weapon requests afterward. 

I repaired this without deleting the Profile/loadout system:

- Pending ped, vehicle, and weapon streaming requests are **no longer immediately released** on the same attempt. The existing code was effectively requesting an asset and then calling `MarkAsNoLongerNeeded()` before a later tick could benefit from that request.
- Background Profile restoration no longer generates a Debug failure for every saved weapon on every retry.
- Manual bulk-loadout attempts now produce one meaningful aggregate pending result rather than potentially dozens/hundreds of individual failures.
- Pending Profile application pauses whenever Dispatch, Convoy, Backup, Gang Incident, Crime Activity, or NPC interaction already owns gameplay. It resumes afterward instead of changing Venti/player model, forcing a vehicle, or processing a huge loadout in the middle of another scene.
- New autonomous Dispatch/Gang/Crime starts are temporarily held while the initial saved Profile assets are still resolving.

For Police Authority, I **did not weaken wanted protection**. The maximum-wanted-level enforcement still executes, but its repetitive runtime evidence is throttled to 30 seconds instead of writing a log every few seconds.

For NPC traffic, the old logic considered **any moving vehicle within 8 m** a collision risk regardless of whether it was actually driving toward you. That explains the enormous amount of collision-guard activity around normal traffic. I changed it so the vehicle must actually be closing on the player, while the frame-level no-collision shield is restricted to an **immediate 3.25 m impact zone**. The scan interval is also relaxed from 350 ms to 500 ms and the temporary shield from 1,400 ms to 900 ms. Passing cars at 5–8 m should therefore stop being constantly interfered with.

For the incomplete traffic-stop sequence, `TrafficPullingOver` is now exempt from the generic 32 m contact-release watchdog while the selected driver is legitimately moving toward the roadside position. There is still an 80 m / 2× traffic-radius escape boundary, so a genuinely lost driver won't remain owned forever.

I found a concrete bug in the current `LSPDBackUp.cs`. `BeginAssetPreparation()` requests the configured Police vehicle and officer models, but the old implementation then releases both models immediately in `finally`; `ProcessAssetPreparation()` does the same thing again. Anyi’s actual game is Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced for PC/Steam, not Legacy. The current installation is C:\Users\Nataniel\STEAM\steamapps\common\Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced. The real ScriptHookVDotNet script directory is C:\Users\Nataniel\STEAM\steamapps\common\Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced\scripts. This is the directory SHVDN actually scans and loads according to the real runtime logs. The correct deployment path for a compiled C# mod is directly inside that scripts directory. Never create scripts\scripts. DLLs and their intended XML/INI configuration files belong directly in the actual scripts directory unless a deliberate subfolder is specifically needed. The game itself has been documented as GTA Enhanced build v3889.0 / 1158, with recent logs identifying build 1158.13. This is the game version to target unless Anyi explicitly supplies a newer verified build.

Anyi’s current machine baseline is an Intel Core i9-11900H laptop CPU, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU, 16 GB RAM, 1920×1080 display, 100 Hz refresh. His current GTA graphics setup can include VSync, DLSS and ray-tracing features. New scripts must therefore be designed around a high-performance laptop with a finite CPU/RAM budget, not around an imaginary desktop with unlimited resources. The performance philosophy is extremely important: UI may need frame-level processing, but expensive world work must be throttled; nearby ped scans should generally be hundreds of milliseconds or several seconds apart depending on their purpose; AI evaluation should generally be roughly 500–1500 ms or slower if possible; maintenance should generally be around 500–1000 ms or several seconds depending on the subsystem; diagnostics should be much slower, often 10–30 seconds; long cooldowns should be used for organic events. Do not scan the entire city every frame, do not create thousands of tick operations, do not repeatedly issue the same task every frame, do not repeatedly write logs every frame, do not create/delete entities unnecessarily, do not keep spawning AI entities simply to simulate activity, and do not make multiple independent AI systems fight for the same ped or vehicle. Anyi’s previous Realistic Road Reaction work established the principle that expensive work must be selective and event/state driven rather than continuous.

The established scripting runtime is ScriptHookV .NET Enhanced 3.9.0.6 with Enhanced runtime/API 1.1.0.6, targeting ScriptHookVDotNet API 3. The active modern assembly is ScriptHookVDotNet3.dll. New work must target API 3 only. The environment may still load older API-2 scripts because they exist in the mod installation, but that is existing compatibility baggage, not a valid target for new development. The new code must use the currently installed API 3 reference and verify actual API members against the installed assembly instead of relying on tutorials or memory. Do not invent classes, methods, properties, enums, task methods or Hash members. When a managed wrapper is unavailable or unreliable, use a verified native call with Function.Call(...), but only after confirming the actual native/API being used. Avoid obsolete members and deprecated wrappers. A known example is that Game.Player.WantedLevel was flagged obsolete in Anyi’s environment; the modern API property is Game.Player.Wanted.WantedLevel. Another known example is that the installed Hash enum did not contain IS_PED_COP or TASK_FLEE_PED, so code should not assume those members exist simply because a tutorial uses them. For flee behavior, SHVDN’s Ped.Task API is preferred when the installed reference exposes the appropriate task method. Any future code must be written against the actual current SHVDN Enhanced API 3 environment, not copied from old GTA V C# tutorials.

The Visual Studio environment is Visual Studio 2022 Community. New mods are created as C# Class Library projects, not EXEs. The normal configuration is Debug | x64, and Anyi does not want the project silently switched to Any CPU because previous reference architecture warnings occurred when Any CPU was mixed with AMD64-oriented assemblies such as LemonUI.SHVDN3 or ScriptHookVDotNet. The normal workflow is Visual Studio → C# Class Library → Debug x64 → add actual references → write .cs source → Build/Rebuild Solution → obtain the compiled .dll from the project output → copy the DLL to the real GTA scripts directory → launch GTA normally → inspect ScriptHookVDotNet.log and the mod’s own log. The green Visual Studio Start button is not the normal way to run the GTA mod because GTA V is the host process. Do not convert the project to an executable. Anyi creates the Visual Studio project himself. The assistant should provide individual .cs, .xml, .ini and connector files to be added to his existing or newly created project; the assistant should not insist on generating a Visual Studio project package or a ready-made .sln/.csproj unless Anyi explicitly requests that.

The core references historically proven in Anyi’s setup include ScriptHookVDotNet3.dll and, when UI is required, LemonUI.SHVDN3.dll. Framework references that have been useful include System, System.Core, System.Drawing, System.IO, System.Runtime.InteropServices, System.Windows.Forms, System.Xml.Linq, System.Net.Http, and related framework assemblies only when actually required by the mod. Existing support assemblies in the installation include NAudio.dll and Newtonsoft.Json.dll, but new mods should reference only the dependencies they actually use. Do not automatically drag all existing DLLs into a new project. Anyi’s current LemonUI architecture uses ObjectPool, NativeMenu, NativeItem and a menu hierarchy built once rather than reconstructed every frame. For UI-based mods, Interval = 0 is the established working pattern because LemonUI requires continuous frame processing. Anyi has had a prior F10 UI flickering problem when a menu architecture was poorly handled. His preferred keyboard approach for robust toggle behavior is GetAsyncKeyState with physical-key polling and rising-edge/debounce logic rather than old KeyDown event toggles. The existing Anyi Partner UI used F10 as its main menu and NumPad0 as a backup, but future mods do not have to reuse those keys unless appropriate; the important part is to preserve the proven physical-key/rising-edge approach when implementing reliable toggles.

The existing script ecosystem is significant and the new mod must coexist with it. It can include or has included AnyiCrimePartner.dll, AnyiRealisticRoadReaction.dll, , Dismemberment.dll, DriverJobs.dll, GangAndTurfMod.dll, iFruitAddon2.dll, LivingLSAIs.dll, PersistencePro.dll, OpenWorldInteriors.dll, LemonUI.SHVDN3.dll, NAudio.dll and Newtonsoft.Json.dll. Some components may be enabled or disabled at different times; historical ASI infrastructure includes Enhanced-compatible tools such as ScriptHookVDotNet.asi, Menyoo.asi, OpenRPF.asi, PackfileLimitAdjusterEnhanced.asi, ModkitLimitAdjusterEnhanced.asi, HeapAdjuster.asi or equivalent current Enhanced variants, DirectStorageFix.asi, DecalPatch.asi, Dynamic Population Density.asi, and other rebuild-dependent ASIs. Never assume historical ASIs are still installed. A new C# mod must not modify, replace, remove or redesign the ASI infrastructure unless Anyi explicitly requests that. Existing Enhanced limit-adjustment infrastructure has included modkit, heap and packfile adjustments, but a new script should never casually tell Anyi to change those values just because the new script exists.

Anyi’s custom ped environment is based heavily on addon/converted Genshin characters. Custom peds may use addon models, custom skeletons and custom textures. A new script must not assume all peds are vanilla GTA freemode models. Proper model loading should follow the familiar validation pattern: create Model, validate it, request/load it, ensure IsLoaded, spawn the entity, and only then assign behavior. Anyi’s established allied companion ped hashes are Shenhe 343272203, Raiden 1957851257, Navia -314526266, Clorinde 834197053, Nefer -1205420430, Arlecchino 1823612999, and Venti -514572009. These seven are Anyi’s own allied companions and should not be automatically classified as hostile gang members, hostile road-reaction targets, or enemies by unrelated scripts. This protection is a hard preference.

The Anyi Partner system is a useful architecture reference but must not be copied wholesale into unrelated mods. It has concepts such as AnyiPartnerScript, ActivePartnerAgent, PartnerDefinition, PartnerMode, PlayerBehavior, DriveMode, ActivePartners, and SelectedPartner, along with support for multiple simultaneous partners, friendly relationships, follow/protection behavior, formations, chauffeur/passenger behavior, recovery, XML weapon loadouts, diagnostics and throttled maintenance. It has previously supported up to 12 active partners. The important transferable design lesson is separation of responsibilities, persistence of state and throttled maintenance, not duplication of the whole partner system.

The Realistic Road Reaction project is another important architectural reference. It explicitly targeted GTA V Enhanced + SHVDN Enhanced API 3 and used throttled world scanning, stored entity references, no unnecessary entity spawning/deletion, no LLAI dependency, event/state-driven reactions and dedicated logging. One major lesson from that project was that a task such as vehicle avoidance should be issued once and allowed to complete instead of reissuing TASK_VEHICLE_DRIVE_WANDER or similar tasks every tick. The Anyi LSPD project should follow the same principle.

Anyi’s Gang & Turf environment is very important to the police project. GangAndTurfMod.dll exists in the GTA scripts directory and uses an external gangModData directory directly under the GTA Enhanced root. The visible directory has GangData.xml, MemberPool.xml, ModOptions.xml, PotentialSpawnsForWars.xml, TurfZoneData.xml, VehiclePool.xml, wipedOutGangsList.xml, and a localization folder. The police mod should not duplicate those files or invent fake “MemberBool” structures; it should consume the actual fields in the real data. Anyi has explicitly said the police mod should be based on the existing GangData and MemberPool data and should use the actual gang-mod directory. The actual current TurfZoneData.xml has 114 turf zones and includes custom territory records suc

h as Davis, Chamberlain Hills, FIB Tower, IAA Tower, Fooliganz Hideout, Bolingbroke Penitentiary, ANYIII, Favonious, and other custom zones. The user’s own gang appears as Anyiii’s Gang in the actual gang data, and one zone shown in the uploaded file is owned by Anyiii's Gang while another is owned by Modstadt's Knight. The data connector should read gang name, gang ownership, member model identifiers, vehicles and turf context. The police system should ask the connector who a nearby suspect or vehicle belongs to, whether the ped is a known gang member, whether the incident is occurring inside a gang territory, and whether the gang belongs to Anyi. It should not modify the GangData XML or fight the Gang & Turf mod’s own behavior. An optional external gang adapter DLL can exist later, but the main Anyi LSPD DLL should be capable of reading the external data directly and should not require an extra adapter just to function.

Logging is a hard part of Anyi’s preferred development workflow. Substantial mods should write their own log directly to the real GTA scripts directory alongside the DLL, never to scripts\scripts. The preferred concept is a dedicated runtime log and, for more complex systems, a report or diagnostic log and an emergency fallback if absolutely necessary. The log should capture boot, configuration, environment, mode changes, dispatch lifecycle, response, entities, tasks, arrests, convoy state, errors, exceptions and stop conditions. It should not write every frame. The log is supposed to answer “what did the mod actually do?” when something behaves incorrectly. Periodic heartbeat entries should be sparse, often 10–30 seconds, and meaningful events should be event-driven. Logs should not be flooded by identical “civilian acknowledges officer” messages every few seconds; persistent per-entity states should prevent repeated duplicate logging.

Historically, Anyi’s GTA setup has gone through careful rebuilds and a stable-baseline methodology. One documented stable check on August 13, 2026 had roughly 45 minutes of GTA gameplay with VSync enabled and high population/traffic density around 80–85%, using Venti as the active player ped and Chaos/explosive gameplay. The broader development philosophy is to rebuild carefully, one mod family at a time, keep a vanilla root separate from mods when necessary, and not allow AI systems to fight over the same world state. Anyi uses a large backup of the GTA installation and wants stability over reckless “fixes” that rewrite the entire environment.

The LSPD project is specifically intended as an immersive, personal Anyi police-roleplay system rather than a total-conversion game. Anyi is not trying to replace GTA V Enhanced or create a completely separate game. He wants a personal police-simulation layer inside his existing Enhanced sandbox, similar in spirit to the roleplay features that players might associate with LSPDFR, but implemented for his own GTA V Enhanced environment through C#, LemonUI, XML/INI and selected external data connectors. He has explicitly said he does not want to make a “different game” from GTA V Enhanced. The goal is to make his own personal mod for ordinary police dispatches, patrols, realistic police response, Gang Anyi behavior, custom ped/vehicle profiles, vanilla or safely verified interiors, evidence, prisoner transport, police interaction and contextual world response.

The LSPD idea has three genuinely different gameplay states. Police Officer Anyi should be a genuine police-authority mode. While on duty, ordinary vanilla law-enforcement should not treat the player as a criminal, and Anyi should not receive ordinary wanted stars merely for being a police officer. The police-authority state should be local to the player and should not globally rewrite the maximum wanted level or permanently destroy all police behavior in the game. Police Officer mode should create its own dispatch, patrol, scene investigation, arrest, transport and officer-interaction layer. The Gang Anyi Territories or Superb Anyi's Gang must be different from Police Authority Mode..

The Police Officer mode should support selectable department/agency, selectable station/interior, selectable officer ped, selectable custom ped model name, selectable police vehicle model name, police profile customization, LSPD/Sheriff/NOOSE/FIB style agency configuration if desired, and configuration through XML/INI rather than hardcoded values. Anyi specifically likes the idea of using his custom polignus vehicle as a police pursuit vehicle. It is treated as a user-provided/custom vehicle model, not assumed to be a verified vanilla GTA police asset. The giant hollow red block that appeared on screen when using the PolIgnus siren is a known gameplay/asset problem. The police logic must not “fix” this by randomly changing native siren parameters or introducing unsupported wrappers. The correct approach is to isolate PolIgnus profile behavior, validate the model, allow emergency lights separately from native siren, and permit NativeSiren=false by configuration until the custom asset’s siren/light setup is explicitly verified. Standard vanilla models such as police, police2, police3, policet and similar verified models remain useful for baseline testing. The first stable test should normally use a known vanilla police vehicle and a known vanilla police ped; PolIgnus can then be enabled as an asset-specific profile once the core is stable.

The police station/interior system should be safe. Anyi wants accessible LSPD locations and interiors from Story Mode and, where safe, Online/DLC content as well, but he explicitly wants research and verification before forcing any interior into the game because he wants to avoid DLC or interior void falling ped  crashes. The current configuration has used Mission Row as the safest primary verified vanilla LSPD interior while other stations may be exterior-safe anchors until their interiors are verified in his exact Enhanced build. Future interior support should be data-driven, with a station registry containing exterior position, heading, interior mode, interior identifier when genuinely verified, optional entry/exit points and NPC placement. Do not blindly install IPL/YMAP/MLO data or force Online interiors just because they exist on a wiki. Do not invent interior names or coordinates. Anything that is not verified in Anyi’s build should be explicitly marked “requires in-game verification” and treated as an exterior-safe option rather than a forced interior.

The police UI is intended to use LemonUI.SHVDN3. Anyi wants something more immersive than a trainer menu. It should include an interaction menu with Duty/Profile, Dispatch/Radio, Station/Interior, Vehicle, Evidence/Inventory, Interaction, Settings and quick GPS. The exact keys can be configurable in the INI, with a proven rising-edge physical-key implementation rather than legacy KeyDown toggles. The menu should be context-sensitive. When no call exists, the Dispatch menu should show availability. When a dispatch is offered, it should present accept/reject. When an incident is active, it should show context-appropriate actions such as approach/investigate, secure suspect, request transport, cancel dispatch, follow convoy, cancel convoy and deliver prisoner. Vehicle menu functionality should support emergency lights, siren mode, doors, radio and radio-station control. Evidence menu should support placing and removing cosmetic evidence markers. Settings should control agency, officer model, vehicle model, station/spawn location, owned apartment if relevant, response settings, police profile and key bindings.

The dispatch system is one of the most important requested features. Anyi wants a real dispatch/callout concept rather than a random mission circle. A dispatch should be offered to the player while on duty, with a bottom-left notification and optionally a minimap blip. It should never use a rigid mission timer. Anyi can be AFK, drive slowly, investigate elsewhere or reject the call. The call has a realistic cooldown after completion or rejection, but the mission itself has no deadline. The player accepts or rejects the call through a configurable key or menu. Accepting should mark the call active and assign a waypoint. The suspect or incident should not disappear simply because Anyi takes time to reach the scene. The call must have explicit lifecycle states such as Offered, Accepted/Active, EnRoute, OnScene, Investigating, SuspectFleeing, SuspectCompliant, SuspectResisting, Arrested, AwaitingTransport, Escorting, Completed, Cancelled, Failed or Compromised. A cancelled dispatch should remove its blip and clean up only entities that the dispatch itself owns. A failed dispatch should have an explicit reason such as suspect deceased, scene invalid, transport destroyed or subject genuinely missing. The previous implementation had a specific bug because organic events were sometimes created directly as Active even though the UI’s acceptance flow expected Offered; this must never happen again. A scene that has an actual fleeing suspect should change to SuspectFleeing rather than simply “subject unavailable.” A dead suspect can become a homicide/investigation scene instead of disappearing. The system should create actual world behavior first and only then promote it to a dispatch where practical: actual vehicle theft, actual reckless driving, actual pedestrian fleeing, actual gang gathering, actual gunfire, actual violent disturbance, etc. It should not simply choose an arbitrary nearby civilian and label him “PedFleeing” without making that person flee.

The requested callout/event variety includes gang pursuits, kidnapping pursuits, vehicle chases, pedestrian pursuits, random criminal meetings, organization activity, vehicle theft or kidnapping, reckless drivers, street disturbances, suspicious meetings, officers responding to incidents, traffic stops and other natural police events. Events should be sparse and contextual rather than constantly appearing. Anyi wants realistic cooldowns, not mission timers. The mod should not generate a new event every few seconds or constantly scan the entire city. A patrol officer should occasionally discover an event while driving or observing the world. Some events may already involve existing GTA entities; others can use managed spawned entities, but if the system spawns a suspect, witness or victim it must explicitly own those entities and maintain them until the incident is completed, cancelled or safely cleaned up.

Police response needs to feel like a real response rather than magic teleportation. Each responding unit should have a patrol origin or station origin, current position, destination, role, current task, call assignment and arrival state. A dispatch should find the nearest suitable available patrol unit or create a new response unit only if capacity allows. The unit should actually drive to the scene. If a suspect already exists, that must not prevent the response vehicle from receiving its drive-to-scene task. A previously observed bug was that response units could be spawned when a subject already existed but were not always commanded to drive, leaving them standing still. This must be corrected in the final implementation. Patrol units should return to patrol after an incident instead of accumulating or vanishing arbitrarily. A unit created by a dispatch should be cleaned up or returned to patrol after the incident ends according to configuration. Normal Anyi mode must not leave custom LSPD units active after exiting police mode; police-owned entities must be cleaned cleanly on mode transition or reset.

Police Officer authority must be explicit. A dedicated authority state should distinguish IsPoliceOfficer, IsGangAuthority, PoliceHostilityDisabled, VanillaWantedPolicy and CustomCrimeLevel. Police Officer mode should establish a protected-authority state so nearby ordinary police do not attack An

yi. The previous code was too blunt because it repeatedly did SET_PLAYER_WANTED_LEVEL = 0, SET_POLICE_IGNORE_PLAYER = true and SET_LAW_PEDS_CAN_ATTACK_NON_WANTED_PLAYER_THIS_FRAME = false every authority refresh, and that approach destroyed too much of GTA’s normal police behavior. The new design must localize the effect to the player’s authority state and ensure police stop targeting Anyi while he is on duty without globally rewriting the world. Normal mode should restore vanilla law enforcement behavior. Gang mode should not permanently disable wanted levels. When Anyi commits actual chaos in Gang mode, wanted levels or a custom equivalent escalation can rise and police can respond intelligently. When Anyi leaves Gang mode, the custom system should cleanly restore the ordinary GTA behavior without leaving permanently modified relationships or dispatch states behind.

Police NPC interaction must feel natural and stateful. The desired state model is something like Normal → Aware → Wary → Approaching → Interacting → Compliant/Resisting/Fleeing/Completed, rather than simply scanning peds every few seconds and repeatedly issuing look or cower tasks. A civilian near Anyi as a police officer can look toward him, move aside, become wary, cower under nearby gunfire, approach for help or provide information/papers in a specific interaction. A police officer encountering an armed Anyi on duty should be able to observe and approach rather than instantly attack him. If Anyi carries a knife or ordinary pistol in normal gameplay, nearby police may watch him, approach, ask him to lower the weapon or investigate. A traffic stop should allow Anyi to approach the driver, attempt to communicate, request documents/papers or identify suspicious behavior. If the driver refuses to stop, the event can escalate into a pursuit. NPCs should not slam their cars into Anyi simply because the script is attempting an interaction. The system needs interaction states, cooldowns and proper stop/approach tasks. The previous implementation was too repetitive and aggressively checked NPCs every scan, producing robotic behavior and repeated “civilian acknowledges Officer Anyi” logs. Persistent per-entity state must prevent duplicate interactions and repeated task issuance.

Arrest behavior must be explicit. A resisting suspect should be able to flee or fight and continue being pursued. A compliant suspect should surrender rather than immediately become “arrested” merely because Anyi pressed one key. The desired visuals include hands-up/cowering behavior, surrender posture, and secured-arrest state with hands behind the back/handcuffed. The interaction should allow Anyi to secure a compliant suspect and then initiate prisoner transport. A suspect who resists and is incapacitated can be treated differently from a suspect who voluntarily surrenders. The callout should not be marked successfully completed simply because the player shot the suspect; the system should decide the outcome based on the incident type and the suspect’s final state. A dead suspect can create an investigation scene rather than an automatic success. An arrested suspect should be explicitly tracked by the custody/convoy system.

The prison convoy is a major requested system and has already failed badly in earlier builds. The proper architecture is a real prisoner-custody state machine: Arrested → Secured → AwaitingTransport → LoadedIntoTransport → Transporting → PrisonArrival → BookIn → Released/Completed. The prisoner must be owned by the convoy manager while transported. The transport vehicle, driver and escort units must be owned by the convoy manager. The prisoner should remain handcuffed and assigned to the transport seat throughout Transporting. Every few seconds, a custody watchdog can verify the prisoner still exists, is still alive, is still in the assigned transport and has not accidentally exited. If GTA somehow ejects or dislodges the prisoner, the system should attempt controlled re-seating. The prisoner should not casually walk out of the convoy van. The prisoner may be intentionally dismounted only at the prison/holding destination or during a configured emergency/compromised state. If the transport vehicle is destroyed, the state should become TransportCompromised and offer recovery rather than leaving a blue marker forever. The convoy should not teleport vehicles beside Anyi and then rely on them to magically escort. The convoy manager should issue driver/escort tasks, maintain spacing without constantly reissuing tasks, and know its destination. The player should be able to cancel the convoy. The prisoner should be booked at the station or prison, and only then should the dispatch/convoy be considered completed. The user has specifically complained that previous convoys stood still, escorts ran away or became robotic, the criminal died, the blue circle remained, the prison was locked, no completion message appeared and the criminal could leave the transport van. All of those are first-class bugs to prevent in the new architecture.

Evidence markers are intended to be cosmetic and immersive, similar to the LSPDFR evidence-marker concept. They can be placed on the ground and removed by interaction. The default model may be configured via XML. Evidence markers should not affect core gameplay unless a future evidence system explicitly adds that. The code must keep the evidence record type in a coherent ownership boundary, preferably in the Evidence subsystem rather than as a mysterious nested type that another source file assumes. The previous implementation suffered from an EvidenceMarkerRecord mismatch between AnyiLSPDEvidence.cs and AnyiLSPDPoliceCore.cs; future files must use one synchronized type definition.

Voice is another intended subsystem. The previous implementation dynamically looked for System.Speech and fell back to subtitles because the assembly was unavailable. That fallback is acceptable during development, but the dispatcher should only speak meaningful radio events. Desired examples include “Unit Anyi, disturbance reported nearby”, “Suspect fleeing on foot”, “Prisoner transport is en route”, and “Unit Anyi, proceed to Mission Row for prisoner transfer.” Voice should not be spammed every tick. If the TTS dependency is unavailable, the script should continue normally with subtitles without crashes.

The police map/icon requirement is explicit. The selected station should have an LSPD icon on the map, and Quick GPS should be able to set waypoints to the nearest police station, prison/jail drop-off, fire station, medical center or another configured point where such points exist. The map/blip logic must have cleanup and should not leave stale blue circles after a cancelled or completed dispatch. Only the currently active incident should own its incident blip. Reset should clean the active blip, owned entities, managed police units, active convoy and stale dispatch state.

The mod should support police departments/agencies such as LSPD, LSSD, NOOSE and FIB through profiles, but these should be configuration choices, not hardwired behaviors. Officer ped models and vehicle models should be configurable, including arbitrary addon ped/vehicle names provided by Anyi. Model loading must validate user-provided models and log invalid/unavailable models cleanly. XML should represent reusable profiles and data rather than hardcoded logic. INI should contain runtime tuning and keybinds. Station XML should contain locations, headings, interior mode and optional interior coordinates. Model XML should contain agency/profile IDs, ped models, vehicle models and emergency-light/siren settings. The user wants the ability to type or change a model name for a custom addon police ped or a custom police vehicle like PolIgnus without recompiling the whole script.

The police vehicle menu should include lights, doors, emergency signals, radio and radio station. The system should not assume every police vehicle has the same door count or the same siren behavior. The previous build hit an API mismatch with VehicleDoorIndex; future door functions must use the exact enum/index type exposed by the installed SHVDN Enhanced API and must not invent an int overload. The vehicle emergency system also previously suffered from a mismatch in ConfigureEmergencyMode(...) signatures. Every caller and callee must come from the same code revision so method signatures remain synchronized. The PolIgnus-specific siren artifact should be controlled through a profile such as EmergencyLights=true, NativeSiren=false until the asset is verified.

The project’s XML/INI architecture should be simple enough for Anyi to understand and edit. The project should not require dozens of external packages or dependencies just to compile. A single AnyiLSPDImmersive.dll is preferred for the core system. Separate DLLs should exist only when there is a genuinely independent subsystem, such as an optional Gang adapter. Multiple .cs files are encouraged for separation of responsibilities but should normally compile into one main DLL. The user explicitly does not want the assistant to create an entire Visual Studio project package; the user wants to create the project himself, add references, then copy or add the individual C# files. The assistant should provide coherent sets of source files from the same revision. Never hand the user a Core from one revision and a World/Evidence/Config file from another revision that expects incompatible signatures.

The major historical development lesson from the previous LSPD iterations is that adding every feature at once made the project unplayable and caused repeated compiler mismatches. Anyi now explicitly wants the assistant to build the project one feature at a time. A new feature must compile before the next one is added. If a feature requires changing several source files, all related files must be provided as one synchronized feature patch. The assistant must account for every changed parameter, field, XML element and parser mapping. If C# produces a warning such as “parameter is unused,” the assistant should decide whether it is an intentional harmless warning, a sign of unfinished logic, or something that should be removed; the user does not want to be told to ignore endless warnings that come from sloppy implementation. The distinction is important: build-blocking errors must be fixed; intentional warnings should be minimized; IDE suggestions are not blockers.

The first milestone for a rebuilt Anyi LSPD system should therefore be deliberately small and stable. It should establish a project that compiles cleanly, loads into GTA, supports Normal Anyi, supports entering/exiting Police Officer mode, establishes local police authority correctly, ensures nearby ordinary police do not attack a legitimate officer, spawns at most one or a very small controlled number of patrol units, supports one configurable police ped and one configurable police vehicle, and maintains a clean mode reset. The first dispatch should then be added as a standalone feature, with accept/reject/cancel, one persistent suspect, proper scene lifecycle, real drive-to-scene behavior and no mission timer. Only after that works should prisoner arrest and transport be added. Then NPC interactions. Then organic events. Then Gang Anyi escalation. Then tactical response. Then military. Then richer interiors and additional callouts. Evidence, voice and optional gang adapter can be introduced at the appropriate feature milestone rather than all at once.

The current project experienced a series of compile errors that should be remembered as examples of what not to repeat. These included missing PatrolPedModel, missing CalloutMinDistance/CalloutMaxDistance, List<string>.Length instead of .Count, undefined ground, VehicleDoorIndex vs int mismatches, float-to-int conversions, VehicleDrivingFlags.Normal being unavailable, Hash.TASK_FLEE_PED being unavailable, Hash.IS_PED_COP

 being unavailable, obsolete Game.Player.WantedLevel, missing OrganicEventRadius, missing MaxNpcReactionsPerScan, missing EvidenceMarkerRecord, mismatched ConfigureEmergencyMode(...) parameters, Action<string,string> callback mismatches, and missing _lastDispatchOffer. These are concrete reminders to verify all members against the actual current references and keep classes synchronized. The recent compilation cycle finally reduced some error counts, but then runtime testing still showed the architecture was unplayable. Do not return to those old patterns.

The runtime logs from the previous LSPD build exposed the most important behavioral failures. The mod successfully loaded GangData, MemberPool and TurfZoneData, so the data connector can work. It could create police vehicles and officers, but it sometimes spawned patrols too frequently and left units active when the player returned to Normal mode. It created organic events and dispatches but sometimes immediately accepted them even when they were intended to be Offered. It could report CALL_FAILED | SubjectUnavailable because the suspect entity was not robustly owned/persisted. It sometimes spawned response units but did not reliably give them drive-to-scene tasks when a subject already existed. It repeatedly logged civilian acknowledgement without remembering that the same pedestrian had already been processed. Gang Anyi could trigger custom response too aggressively, sometimes producing a severity 5 response and SWAT immediately instead of the intended gradual escalation. Voice often fell back because System.Speech was unavailable. The reset function could clean units, but simply switching to Normal did not always clean them. These behaviors demonstrate why the next build must be stateful and ownership-driven.

The current police interaction philosophy should be “natural world simulation” rather than “mission manager.” A civilian should not suddenly freeze or become a task dummy because Anyi walked near them. A police officer should not attack Anyi because the mod failed to synchronize authority with vanilla police logic. A traffic offender should not ram Anyi merely because the AI task was constantly reissued. A suspect should not disappear because Anyi took thirty seconds to arrive. A prison convoy should not exist only as a set of spawned vehicles; it should be a persistent stateful operation. A dispatch marker should disappear when cancelled and a scene should remain coherent until its final state. A patrol officer should not repeatedly react to the same pedestrian or scan the same gang member every second.

When discussing external references, Anyi has explicitly requested that the GTA model/hash information for police, places/interiors, vehicles, weapons and peds be based on https://gtahash.com/, but that source must be treated carefully and its exact data should not be presented as guaranteed Enhanced metadata unless verified. Logging is a hard part of Anyi’s preferred development workflow. Substantial mods should write their own log directly to the real GTA scripts directory alongside the DLL, never to scripts\scripts. Historically, Anyi’s GTA setup has gone through careful rebuilds and a stable-baseline methodology.
